title: Effects of forearm rotation on wrist flexor and extensor muscle activities.

use: At controlled torque: ECRB higher with pronation; FCR higher with supination; FCU lower pronated than neutral; ECU not different. Analog for wrist variants only.

title: Electromyographic activity and strength during maximum isometric pronation and supination efforts in healthy adults.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Fine-wire pronation/supination: PT/PQ pronate, supinator/biceps supinate; deep PQ may stabilize in both. Not isolation percentages.

title: Characterizing forearm muscle activity in university-aged males during dynamic radial-ulnar deviation of the wrist using a wrist robot.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Robot-based dynamic deviation experiment: posture, direction and phase affect activation/co-contraction. Not dumbbell-specific allocation.

title: The effects of isometric hand grip force on wrist kinematics and forearm muscle activity during radial and ulnar wrist joint perturbations.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Increasing grip force increased most recorded forearm activity, including wrist extensors, during perturbations. Not carry/hang percentage calibration.

title: Muscular coordination of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion with respect to hand position.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Elbow flexion hand position changes BR activation; small acute study. No long-term hypertrophy ranking.

title: Impact of Fat Grip Attachments on Muscular Strength and Neuromuscular Activation During Resistance Exercise.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Thick grips reduced strength performance and increased forearm EMG in some tested lifts, not all. No universal thick-grip multiplier.

title: Selective recruitment of single motor units in human flexor digitorum superficialis muscle during flexion of individual fingers.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: FDS motor units show selective recruitment across fingers. Whole-muscle grip allocation cannot resolve all digits.

title: Neither load nor systemic hormones determine resistance training-mediated hypertrophy or strength gains in resistance-trained young men.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Trained-men trial: 20–25 versus 8–12 reps to failure produced similar hypertrophy outcomes; not isolated forearm-muscle data.

title: Effects of different intensities of resistance training with equated volume load on muscle strength and hypertrophy.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Trial comparing 20/40/60/80% 1RM: very low load underperformed, higher loads favored strength. Not precise forearm rep optima.

title: Cross-education after high-frequency versus low-frequency volume-matched handgrip training.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Small four-week isometric handgrip study: volume-matched frequencies both improved grip; forearm thickness changes do not identify each muscle response.

title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains.

use: 67-study meta-regression: distinguishing direct and indirect sets helped fit; diminishing returns. Fractional 0.5 is not validated for each small forearm muscle.

title: Exploring the Dose-Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Series of Meta-Regressions.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Exploratory meta-regressions associate closer failure with more hypertrophy; exact relationship uncertain. Do not compute precise effective-rep bonuses.

title: Isometric training and long-term adaptations: Effects of muscle length, intensity, and intent: A systematic review.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Review: isometric adaptations depend on length, intensity and intent. No universal seconds-to-dynamic-set conversion.

title: Mechanical, Material and Morphological Adaptations of Healthy Lower Limb Tendons to Mechanical Loading: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Loading adapts tendon properties in lower-limb evidence. Not forearm injury thresholds; force/strain cannot be inferred from logged kg alone.

title: The association between combination of hand force and forearm posture and incidence of lateral epicondylitis in a working population.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Occupational prospective study links combinations of force and posture with lateral epicondylitis. Workshift hazard ratios cannot become gym injury probabilities.

title: Quantitative Measures of Physical Risk Factors Associated with Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders of the Elbow: A Systematic Review.
access: PubMed abstract and metadata; not a full-text systematic review
use: Review of work-related elbow risk factors. Population/exposure context limits transfer to training.

use: Meta-analysis: higher loads favor 1RM strength; hypertrophy occurs across loading ranges in studied conditions. Not a muscle-specific optimal rep table.
